abstract.t: The resumable upload protocol lets a client continue an interrupted upload, but the upload has to be sent in order, one request at a time. This document extends that protocol so that a client can send different parts of the same upload in parallel. Servers and intermediaries can limit both the number of concurrent requests and the amount of data that arrives out of order. The document also describes how intermediaries that inspect uploads (for data loss prevention or malware scanning, say) can continue to do so, and how the extension behaves over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3.
